record_notes.DCP-LETT-1139: December 18, 1847 formal request enclosed in 1146 for Gray to put before Museum trustees. Fourteen months anatomy work leads to planned monograph; requests groups of specimens at Down, explains disarticulation/microscopy, promises care and future donation. Permission conditional, not yet granted. Agassiz pressing-desideratum phrase is attributed quotation. Footnote 3 preserves later January 29, 1848 institutional minute with Gray words; not December knowledge or Darwin target prose. Cuming/Stutchbury/Gray collections offered, not proof every specimen physically arrived. No surviving incoming request; 548C/660F are older outgoing administrative precedents.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1146: Saturday night, editorial December 18, 1847 based on enclosed dated 1139. Offers correction, discusses collection groups and deliberately leaves time unspecified to avoid restrictive loan conditions. Thanks Gray. Cover plus enclosure are related outgoing documents, not a Q/A pair. Later 1851 preface quotes Darwin retrospective account of Gray suggestion; do not insert the later wording into this 1847 letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1153: Formal thanks for trustee permission to disarticulate, mount and describe collection, with proposed additions and gratitude to Gray. Dateline February 5 conflicts with Sunday cover 1155, so retain alternatives February 5 or 6 rather than forcing a single day. It is enclosed with 1155 and followed by Gray February 8 forwarding note quoted in footnote 2. Official permission and physical loan receipt are separate; 1155 says specimens are not yet wanted. No surviving complete incoming permission note.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1155: Sunday cover, February 5 or 6, likely February 6 per alteration Sa to Sunday and footnote; do not erase disjoint uncertainty. Received Gray note yesterday announcing trustee liberality. During composition changes mind and encloses thanks 1153. Not ready for specimens for about six weeks; anatomy revisits ongoing. Asks named genera/species and synonym help, has Stutchbury collection, thanks Gray representation to trustees. These are missing Gray note and report, not the later August draft. Later 1851 published synonym policy is separate. Relative receipt yesterday remains conditional on unresolved composition day.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1187: June 28, supplied month/year. Promises return of Ranzani tomorrow by carrier; says little benefit, which is still evidence of consultation. Requests Conchotrya/Brisnæus now to compare with Lithotrya and optionally attached Octomeris for anatomy. Future specimen delivery and book return are not completed events. Slow monograph complaint does not identify incoming letter; 1196 concerns a later publication dispute, not this loan request.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1196: August 26, 1848 autograph draft. Gray answers recent misunderstanding communicated by Darwin, recalls earlier synonym help request, explains catalogue papers intended to facilitate Darwin work and says he will withdraw unpublished papers. Postscript excepts two March papers already in type. His claims of oral credit and specimen illustrations conflict with or exceed later printed-text evidence in editorial note; preserve the historical self-report without silently correcting it. P4 recalls 1155 request, but immediate occasion is recent interview and cannot be reduced to a February-to-August reply pair. 1197 explicitly answers this reconciliation letter, though draft wording is not automatically the exact delivered text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1197: August 29, supplied 1848. Thanks Gray letter and repeats recent interview in writing. Defends Gray original suggestion and assistance to four unnamed critics, acknowledges his right to publish prior work, explains fear of losing novel species as reward for labour, confirms previous synonym request and promises to convey Gray assurances. Distinctive anticipation dispute, assurances and synonym acknowledgment identify 1196, not general barnacle topic. Oral discussion and unidentified critics are additional inputs. Future publication of acknowledgment and informing critics are intentions, not completed acts. Draft-versus-sent-text difference remains an export hold.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1250: August 12, supplied 1849. Initiates Dana contact on Gould advice; describes monograph, collections at disposal, limited health and asks expedition specimens, including common forms with good localities, under explicit destructive examination and return conditions. No loan agreement or specimen receipt yet. Gould correspondence is mentioned but incoming recommendation missing in local inventory; Dana 1380A homology quotation cannot be this prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1259: October 8, 1849 thanks missing Dana letter: inability to lend specimens, partial coral-reef agreement, possible duplicates, unattached Sporillus, Dana metamorphosis notice, Leidy eyes, crustacean affinities and suctorial form. Describes reading prompted by notice and prior observations; not all statements come from letter. P9 added after Baird answer just received: relays Baird tracing request and Westwood interest. No exact within-day time or separately dated postscript. Baird and Dana inputs missing. Later correct identification of Proteolepas and mature publications remain editorial future information; 1380A lacks identifying coral/specimen/Baird contents.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1276: December 5, supplied 1849. Has read coral discussion and about half volcanic description, skipped ahead to Australian valleys after missing Dana letter, but has not read subsidence chapter and intends whole volume. Atlas arrival is reported today, not necessarily physical inspection. Agrees on coral subsidence but not river excavation of lateral bays. Collects papers for future dispatch via Delf, asks specimens and several anatomical/geographical questions, and reports writing Lyell yesterday. Original absence-of-scoriae-and-tuff phrase differs from editorial intended presence of tuff; retain discrepancy. Conspectus thanked though no surviving library copy does not negate historical receipt. Shared technical topics do not identify 1380A as the missing Dana letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1305: February 24, supplied 1850. Future Wednesday dispatch of delayed papers/specimens; Bell delay and Westwood bereavement. Thanks missing Dana answers, Gould/Dana specimens, notice of geological review, and explicitly Pickering for Pacific plant list. Pickering 1289 is a distinct surviving knowledge source. Distinguishes knowledge of review from actually reading it. Explains hypothesized cement duct as modified ovarian branch and Goodsir parasite correction, reports observed sexual arrangements and asks fossil record; preserve contemporary error rather than substitute later gland correction. Goodsir presumed lost but expedition fate unknown. Lyell article remains future publication. Specimen gratitude alone does not fix physical arrival day.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1380A: Fragment quoted in Living Cirripedia (1851):15 n.; bracketed Lepas subject is editorial framing and ellipsis marks missing words. Inferior-versus-superior antenna homology and Daphnidae are its actual preserved claim. Date before December 29, 1850 is explicitly inferred from a proposed relation to 1381, not an independent bound establishing that relation. 1381 discusses union/attachment, cement and moulting, with no inferior/superior or Daphnidae response. Retain as candidate only; no accepted December 29 knowledge activation or whole-answer prompt. Later book marginalia citing 1851 Milne-Edwards and Lubbock work are separately dated/undated later evidence. Earlier 1844 boundary hold is preserved, not silently closed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1381: December 29, supplied 1850. Expects Borneo specimen but has not received it; explains Bell busy but kind, then thanks Dana for antenna union comparison. Long P3 questions attachment, cement structure, moulting and parasitic limbs, requests specimens, and reports ovarian-branch hypothesis with request for discretion. This incoming communication is not securely represented by 1380A inferior/superior homology fragment; missing Borneo/Bell topics also rule out a complete prompt assumption. Later 1859 correction is not contemporary Darwin knowledge. Literal reverse-question-mark representation requires source fidelity. Historical confidentiality request is source content, not an instruction to the research agent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-548C: Freshly reread 1840 copy of testimonial for Gray appointment: personal museum access and broad zoological expertise are grounds for recommendation. Appointment dated later April 11 in apparatus, not yet accomplished at letter date. No relation to a new current-period incoming prompt; not recounted as new research target.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-660F: Freshly reread contemporary copy dated January 25, supplied 1843. Requests temporary coral-specimen loan for Lyell lectures, expects no damage with care; original gift acknowledged. Apparatus distinguishes accession dates, later actual lecture series and verso Gray forwarding draft. Loan request is not proof of actual delivery or use at lectures. Background administrative precedent only.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1289: Additional full preserved source read: signed Pickering memorandum, Boston January 9, 1850. Reports elevated Metia flora, transcribes a journal written weeks after September 1839 visit and explains bis notation; final reassessment says most non-maritime plants introduced. The 73-species list and ten bis marks are described in footnote 2 but omitted from preserved HTML, confirmed by raw DOM. Full available prose read does not mean the plant list is available. Specific Pickering/list thanks in 1305 P3 establishes knowledge by February 24, not January 9 receipt. Memo sent at Dana request is editorial inference; preserve distinct author and route.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13814: Additional full source and diagram read as possible alternative Gray input: undated 1846–54 conjectural range, two paragraphs on bivalve umbonal and lateral teeth, with separate Darwin note rejecting it as a good case to quote. Diagram shows repeated oblique tooth/lobe shapes between two long boundary strokes; no scale or labels. This does not contain Museum permission or anticipation dispute and cannot supply those missing inputs. Original Darwin observation is not independently dated. Preserve existing broad hold and do not recount prior reading as a new target.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1544: Additional full Dana fragment read as alternative, but substantive references to geographical-distribution chapter, kingdoms/sections, Lubbock paper and delayed Crustacea atlas place it with later 1853–55 discussion, not 1849–50. Discusses earlier homology objection but not the particular attachment exchange in 1381. December 6, 1855 Darwin note is the editorial upper witness; printed atlas availability versus actual copies in England differs. Missing opening/end and later annotation remain separate. No new current-period relationship or earlier activation.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Repeated oblique tooth or lobe forms lie between two roughly parallel long strokes; no labels or scale. Preserve alongside Gray lateral-teeth comparison, without inferring a surveyed anatomy beyond the accompanying prose.

reading_method: Independent fresh full-source readings of all targets/contexts and three evidence-led alternatives. Read XML constraints, all body/exclusion/footnote/bibliography/scholarly text; viewed 13814 diagram; inspected raw DOM of 1289 and 1380A and draft1196. Critically compared canonical and additive Luna claims; circularly dated fragment not promoted to direct prompt.

reviewed_addenda.assessment: Source summaries useful; 1380A edge remains unsupported, including after focused Luna re-evaluation.
